executive_summary: The dominant thread running through today's content is the accelerating U.S.-Iran confrontation, which connects the breaking news of fresh American strikes on southern Iranian targets to both The Economist's newsletter flagging that Iran talks are 'coming under fire' and Foreign Affairs' strategic prescription to 'Let Iran Defeat Itself.' This convergence is significant because it reveals a sharp tension between diplomatic and military tracks happening simultaneously — the U.S. is striking Iranian targets even as negotiations appear to be fracturing, suggesting Washington may be abandoning a strategy of coercive diplomacy in favor of direct military pressure. Foreign Affairs' framing of allowing Iran to collapse under its own contradictions now reads as a road not taken, making its publication today particularly pointed. The stakes are high: escalation with Iran carries direct implications for regional stability, global energy markets, and U.S. strategic positioning at a moment when its foreign policy bandwidth is already stretched across multiple theaters.

items.headline: Our Summer Cooking List: 24 Fresh Recipes to Seize the Season
items.blurb: While summer technically lasts a little more than a quarter of the year, the time to grill outside, indulge in perfect peaches and dreamy heirloom tomatoes, or just eat a hot dog, sand in your hair, feels fleeting. You want to make every bite count. We consider these 24 recipes our summer bucket list, our must-makes, full of bright produce and opportunities to be outside. Make as many you can, at your own leisurely pace, before the sun sets on the season.

items.headline: Knicks sweep Cavs, head to NBA Finals
items.blurb: The New York Knicks are returning to the NBA Finals for the first time since 1999. Last night's 130-93 drubbing of the Cleveland Cavaliers completed a sweep in which the Knicks were plus-77 for the four-game series. New York has now won 11 playoff games in a row. Only four other teams in NBA history have done that in a single postseason. The 1999 San Antonio Spurs (12 straight), 2001 Los Angeles Lakers (11), and 2017 Golden State Warriors (15) all won championships using these streaks. Only the 1989 Lakers (11 in a row) failed to win the title.

items.headline: The Knicks can win the NBA championship this year
items.blurb: But make no mistake. The Knicks can win the NBA championship this year. It wouldn't take some catastrophic injury, either. New York has a good enough offense and a good enough defense to get this done. The team has discovered a new gear during this 11-game win streak.

items.headline: Tensions rise in L.A.
items.blurb: The 30 or so minutes of practice the media gets to view aren't always the most revelatory. But there was some actual tension at practice in Los Angeles last week after the Sparks, who came into the season with hopes of contention, started the season 1-3. After the scout team scored on yet another offensive rebound, Nneka Ogwumike had about enough. She chastised her teammates for relaxing after every mistake instead of continuing to play. Ionescu made her season debut against the Dallas Wings on Sunday, finishing with 11 points, seven assists and five rebounds in the Liberty's 91-76 loss. newsletters.title: A reality check on the AI jobs hysteria

items.headline: A reality check on the AI jobs hysteria
items.blurb: Despite the growing hysteria over AI's threat to white-collar jobs, there's still scant evidence that the technology has had a large-scale impact on the labor market. Analysis of US labor data shows that unemployment in occupations most exposed to AI is actually lower than in less-exposed jobs. There are also no signs that large numbers of workers are shifting from AI-threatened professions into supposedly safer manual-labor jobs. It's true that things aren't great in the job market—but the question is why.

items.headline: Opinion: It's time to address the looming crisis in entry-level work
items.blurb: AI has not yet produced mass unemployment. But it may be quietly weakening the first rung of the career ladder. A recent Stanford study found that young workers in AI-exposed occupations suffered a sharp decline in employment after the spread of generative AI. The same pattern didn't appear in low-exposure jobs, suggesting AI is replacing junior tasks that once gave young workers their first foothold. It's time to rethink how we train, prepare, and support young people entering the workforce.

items.headline: The Pope has called for governments to regulate AI
items.blurb: In his first major document, Pope Leo said AI must be "disarmed." He warned that AI fuels war and misinformation, but could also "open up a horizon extending in all directions." Anthropic cofounder Chris Olah also spoke at the event.

items.headline: SpaceX has launched its biggest and most powerful rocket
items.blurb: The Starship V3 made its test flight debut two days after Elon Musk announced SpaceX's IPO. SpaceX pulled off the launch, but not the landing. The rocket could be key to SpaceX's valuation, but rivals to the company are rising.

items.headline: Huawei says it can make industry-leading chips within five years
items.blurb: The Chinese tech giant announced a breakthrough in chip design. Its progress underscores Beijing's push to neutralize US sanctions. Chinese chip stocks rallied after the announcement.

items.headline: A new vaccine may protect against the Ebola virus behind today's crisis
items.blurb: Tests have shown promising results for the mRNA vaccine. Another Ebola vaccine could be ready for trials in months. But vaccines face a new problem: their name.

items.headline: America carried out new air strikes on Iran
items.blurb: US Central Command said it had struck missile sites in the south of the country and boats laying mines, in what it called an act of self-defence "to protect our troops" during an "ongoing ceasefire". Donald Trump has spent days suggesting a deal is near, though he also warned negotiators "not to rush". Iran said talks had advanced, but that an agreement was "not imminent".

items.headline: Mr Trump faces another test of his grip on the Republican Party in a Texas primary run-off
items.blurb: John Cornyn, the incumbent senator, is fighting to fend off Ken Paxton, the state's attorney-general, whom Mr Trump endorsed last week. Some Republicans fear Mr Paxton's legal troubles—including an impeachment by fellow Republicans—could make him a weaker candidate against James Talarico, the Democrats' well-funded nominee, in November's midterms.

items.headline: Court documents showed that Nasire Best, a man accused of opening fire near the White House, had previously been detained twice by the Secret Service
items.blurb: Court documents showed that Nasire Best, a man accused of opening fire near the White House on Saturday, had previously been detained twice by the Secret Service after trying to enter the building. Mr Best allegedly wounded a bystander before the Secret Service shot and killed him. During one of the earlier incidents he told officers he was Jesus Christ.

items.headline: Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents pepper-sprayed Andy Kim, a Democratic senator from New Jersey
items.blurb: Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents pepper-sprayed Andy Kim, a Democratic senator from New Jersey, during his visit to Delaney Hall, a migrant detention centre in the state. Around 300 of those held there are on a work and hunger strike, demanding the release of elderly, young and sick inmates. Protesters had gathered outside to try to stop the transfer of the strike's organiser, Martin Soto; officials said they moved him to another facility.

items.headline: Firefighters said they had eliminated the threat of explosion posed by a damaged chemical tank in Orange County, California
items.blurb: Some 50,000 residents of Garden Grove, a city south of Los Angeles, were evacuated after the tank, which contains methyl methacrylate, a flammable substance used to make plastic, overheated on Thursday. Around 16,000 people are still unable to return home.

breaking_digest.narrative:
The United States carried out new strikes in southern Iran [3], marking the latest escalation in ongoing military operations against Iranian targets. No immediate details were released on the scope or objectives of the strikes, but the action signals continued U.S. military engagement in the region. Separately, a federal court rejected Alabama's newly drawn congressional map, ruling it remains unfair to Black voters [1]. The decision, which follows earlier Supreme Court-mandated redistricting efforts, keeps pressure on state lawmakers to produce a map that adequately represents the state's Black population.

On the sports front, the New York Knicks completed a sweep of the Cleveland Cavaliers to advance to the N.B.A. Finals [2], closing out the Eastern Conference series in four games. The Knicks' berth in the Finals marks a significant milestone for a franchise that has not competed for a championship in decades.
